import pandas as pd

# Source file paths
source_files = [
    "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length1_92/training_0.csv"
]

# List to hold dataframes from all sources
dfs = []

for file_path in source_files:
    # Read each source CSV, ignoring the first index column (index_col=0)
    df = pd.read_csv(file_path, index_col=0)
    
    # Normalize column names to lowercase for safety (optional)
    df.columns = [col.strip() for col in df.columns]
    
    # According to the target schema, ensure columns are exactly ['user_id', 'email', 'geo']
    # Source schema matches target schema, so no renaming needed.
    # But user_id values in source start with uppercase 'User_' while target examples show lowercase 'user_'
    # Normalize user_id to lowercase to match target examples format.
    df['user_id'] = df['user_id'].str.lower()
    
    # Append to list
    dfs.append(df)

# Since all source tables have the same schema as the target, union (concat) all dataframes
target_df = pd.concat(dfs, ignore_index=True)

# Ensure columns are in the order of target schema
target_df = target_df[['user_id', 'email', 'geo']]

# Write the result to the target path
target_df.to_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length1_92/target_multisource.csv", index=False)
